module_title: Types of Ores, Major Mines, and Industrial Uses
introduction: At this level, we differentiate between the grades of iron ore, locate India's most famous mining centers, and understand the economic significance of minerals like Copper, Mica, and Manganese.

core_concepts.title: Varieties of Iron Ore
core_concepts.description: 1. Magnetite: The finest quality iron ore with a very high iron content (up to 70%). It has excellent magnetic qualities. 2. Hematite: The most important 'industrial' iron ore. It has a slightly lower iron content (50-60%) but is used in massive quantities.

core_concepts.title: Major Iron Ore Mines
core_concepts.description: Bailadila (Chhattisgarh): Produces high-grade hematite that is exported to Japan and South Korea. Kudremukh (Karnataka): Known to be one of the largest iron ore deposits in the world.

core_concepts.title: Copper
core_concepts.description: India is critically deficient in the reserve and production of copper. Being malleable, ductile, and a great conductor, it is heavily used in electrical cables and electronics. Major mines: Khetri (Rajasthan), Balaghat (Madhya Pradesh), and Singhbhum (Jharkhand).

core_concepts.title: Mica
core_concepts.description: A non-metallic mineral made up of a series of plates or leaves. Because of its excellent di-electric strength, low power loss, and insulating properties, it is indispensable in the 'electric and electronic industries'. 'Andhra Pradesh' (Nellore belt) is the largest producer.

important_entities.name: Manganese
important_entities.significance: Manganese is primarily used in the manufacturing of steel and ferro-manganese alloys. It takes nearly 10 kg of manganese to manufacture one tonne of steel. Odisha and Madhya Pradesh are the top producers.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: If the exam asks: 'Which is the BEST quality iron ore?' (Answer: Magnetite). If the exam asks: 'Which is the MOST IMPORTANT / highly used iron ore in India?' (Answer: Hematite).

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: The 'Khetri' mines in Rajasthan are historically (since the Harappan civilization) and currently the most famous copper mines in India.

exam_strategy_tips: Direct matching questions are frequent: Bailadila -> Chhattisgarh, Kudremukh -> Karnataka, Khetri -> Rajasthan.
If a question asks which mineral easily splits into thin sheets/leaves and is an excellent insulator, the answer is always 'Mica'.
